title: Compare Gaussian means, shapes, and volume

blocks.text: Two Gaussians can disagree in several ways. Their centers can differ, their spreads can point along different axes, or their occupied volumes can differ. The formula combines these effects. The animation uses two-dimensional diagonal covariances so you can see each component without needing a full matrix visualization of correlations.

KL divergence measures the dissimilarity between two probability distributions. In this problem, you'll implement a function to compute the KL divergence between two multivariate Gaussian distributions given their means and covariance matrices. Use the provided mathematical formulas and numerical considerations to ensure accuracy.

A multivariate Gaussian describes a vector using a mean and covariance. The covariance captures spread and correlation. KL divergence is an expected log-density ratio: it measures the mismatch when observations from P are described using Q. It is directed, not a metric.

The displacement of the means is measured through Q’s inverse covariance. Moving one unit along a direction where Q is narrow is more surprising than moving one unit along a direction where Q is wide. This is the Mahalanobis mean term. Change the mean separation while keeping the covariances fixed to isolate this contribution.

blocks.text: The trace term compares the spread of P to that of Q. The log determinant ratio compares their volumes. The dimension correction balances those terms so identical distributions have zero divergence. Individual terms can be negative; their final sum is nonnegative for valid nonsingular covariance matrices, apart from small numerical error. Do not interpret each term as a separate distance.

The supplied solution explicitly computes determinants and an inverse. That is adequate for the tiny examples shown, but a numerically robust implementation often uses log-determinants and linear solves instead. Both covariance matrices must be symmetric positive definite for this ordinary density formula. Singular Gaussian cases require separate treatment. The examples verify the formula against the preserved solution, including the zero result when P equals Q. Natural logarithms make the units nats.

checks.prompt: If both means and covariance matrices are identical, what is KL(P || Q)?

explanation.correct: The log-volume and mean terms vanish; the trace equals the dimension and cancels the subtraction.

checks.prompt: For one-dimensional Gaussians with equal variance 1 and means separated by 2, what is KL in nats?

explanation.correct: Only the mean term remains: one half times 2² is 2.
